name: marquee-css
summary: Infinite logo/testimonial ticker band running Magic UI's marquee keyframes: two rows scrolling opposite ways, edge-masked, pausable on hover, and entirely CSS.

duration.description: One full traverse of a row. Upstream's [--duration:40s] on the outer div.

gap.description: Space between items and between the repeated rows. Upstream's [--gap:1rem]. Must be a length: the keyframes translate by calc(-100% - gap), which a unitless value makes invalid.

pauseOnHover.description: Pause every row while the pointer is over the band. Upstream's group-hover:[animation-play-state:paused].

deviations.what: The React component is gone. Its Tailwind utility classes are written out as CSS, and Array(repeat).fill(0).map(...) is four copies of the row in snippet.html.
deviations.why: paw-fx is vanilla and a generated site has no build step, so there is no React and no Tailwind compiler to produce the classes at runtime.

deviations.what: Upstream's var(--gap) and var(--duration) are var(--fx-gap) and var(--fx-duration). The keyframe bodies are otherwise verbatim, including calc(-100% - var(--fx-gap)).
deviations.why: The effect contract requires custom properties to be prefixed --fx-.

deviations.what: The band carries a linear-gradient mask so the rows fade out at both edges, which upstream does not do.
deviations.why: Upstream demos the component inside a bordered card, where the hard cut reads as the card edge. A full-bleed section has no such edge and the cut reads as clipped content.

deviations.what: The reverse switch is a markup class (.fx-marquee__band--reverse) rather than a mount option.
deviations.why: Upstream's reverse is per-Marquee and the section holds two of them going opposite ways, so it belongs to the row, not to the section mount() is handed.
